title: Impersonal 2: Нужно and Надо (necessity)
description: Russian builds everyday necessity with two near-synonyms: нужно and надо. The slot is the same as можно or нельзя: an optional dative person, the necessity word, and an infinitive. This lesson adds the не нужно / не надо soft negation and the past было / future будет tense words.
descriptionRussian: Русский язык выражает повседневную необходимость двумя почти синонимами: «нужно» и «надо». Структура такая же, как у можно или нельзя: лицо в дательном падеже (по желанию), слово необходимости, инфинитив. Здесь добавляем мягкое отрицание «не нужно / не надо» и слова времени «было» (прошедшее) и «будет» (будущее).
intro: The same frame with a different word in the middle, which is the point: once you have the shape, each new lesson is vocabulary. Worth noticing is what the negation does here. Saying there is no need is a much softer thing than saying something is forbidden, and Russian uses different words for the two where English uses 'don't have to' and 'must not'.
rules: Structure: (dative person, optional) + нужно or надо + infinitive. Same slot as можно and нельзя. The person it applies to is always in the dative, never the nominative.
Нужно and надо are near-synonyms for necessity. Надо is a little more casual, нужно a little more neutral; both work in everyday speech.
Negation: не нужно or не надо, both meaning 'no need to.' This is softer than нельзя, which is a firm 'forbidden.'
Past adds было; future adds будет. Both sit in the fixed neuter form (было / будет) and never change for the gender of the dative person: Маше нужно было идти, Нам нужно будет идти.

Word order is flexible: нужно было and было нужно are both correct (нужно было is a bit more common). The infinitive's aspect follows the usual rule - perfective for one bounded act, imperfective for a habit or process.
examples: Мне нужно идти. (I need to go.) Dative мне; necessity word нужно; imperfective infinitive идти.
Антону надо отдохнуть. (Anton needs to rest.) Dative Антону; necessity word надо; perfective infinitive отдохнуть.
Не надо так говорить. (No need to say that.) Soft negation with не; no dative person; imperfective infinitive говорить.
Маше нужно было купить хлеб. (Masha needed to buy bread.) Past with было; perfective infinitive купить.
Завтра нам нужно будет встать рано. (Tomorrow we will need to get up early.) Future with будет; perfective infinitive встать.
Нужно много читать, чтобы хорошо знать язык. (One needs to read a lot to know the language well.) Generic necessity; no dative person.

items.promptEnglish: You must not talk loudly in the library.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: prohibition word for a generic rule.
items.explanation: Нельзя is the prohibition word from Lesson 1, the right fit for a posted rule. Нужно and надо would mean 'one needs to talk loudly,' which makes no sense as a library rule. Хочу is the verb 'I want,' which would need a personal subject (я), not an impersonal construction.

items.promptEnglish: I need to go, it is already late.
items.hint: Necessity in a personal frame: a dative person plus an infinitive.
items.explanation: Нужно expresses necessity with the dative мне and the infinitive идти. Должна would build a personal-subject sentence ('I (fem) must go') and would need я in the nominative. Хочется belongs to Lesson 5 and reads as 'I feel like going,' not 'I need to.' Можно is permission, the wrong meaning.

items.promptEnglish: Anton needs to rest after work.
items.hint: Necessity in an impersonal frame with a dative person.
items.explanation: Надо expresses necessity; the dative Антону names the person it applies to. Хочет, может, and должен are personal-subject words that would require Антон in the nominative, not the dative. The impersonal slot is the structure this lesson drills.

items.promptEnglish: No need to say that, it is rude.
items.hint: Soft 'no need to.' Which necessity word pairs with не to soften a request?
items.explanation: Не надо is the standard soft negation ('no need to, please don't'). Нельзя would be a firm ban ('forbidden'), too strong here. Не можно is ungrammatical. Не хочу is 'I do not want,' a personal-subject sentence, not impersonal.

items.hint: Past tense word in an impersonal sentence. Which fixed form?
items.explanation: Impersonal sentences use the fixed neuter было in the past, no matter the gender of the dative person. Был (masc) and была (fem) would require a personal nominative subject. Будет is the future word, the wrong tense for the English 'needed.'

items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow we will need to get up early.
items.hint: Future tense word in an impersonal sentence.
items.explanation: 'Will need to' is future, so the future word is будет in its fixed neuter form, with nothing to agree with. Было would be past, contradicting 'завтра.' Был and была are past forms for personal subjects, wrong in an impersonal sentence.

items.promptEnglish: Yesterday I had to work late.
items.hint: Shift нужно into the past: which tense word joins it?
items.explanation: The past of impersonal нужно adds the frozen neuter было: нужно было работать. Была would try to agree with a subject the frame does not have; будет is the future.

items.promptEnglish: Masha will need to call the doctor tomorrow.
items.hint: Shift надо into the future: which tense word?
items.explanation: The future of impersonal надо adds будет: надо будет позвонить. Было is the past, clashing with 'завтра'; есть is not used in this frame.

items.prompt: Тебе _____ отдыхать, ты совсем не устал.
items.promptEnglish: You don't need to rest - you aren't tired at all.
items.hint: A soft 'no need to': which negation?
items.explanation: The soft negation is не нужно ('no need to'): тебе не нужно отдыхать. Нельзя would FORBID resting, a much stronger claim; the не comes before нужно, not after.

blanks: Мне _____ идти, уже поздно. (I need to go, it is already late.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The English 'need to' is necessity, the standard reading of нужно. Должна would require я in the nominative (personal-subject 'I must'). Можно is permission. Хочется (Lesson 5) is 'I feel like,' a different reading.

sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative person + necessity word + infinitive + object. Present tense, so no было or будет.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Anton needs to rest after work.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative Антону + надо + perfective infinitive. Present tense.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Masha needed to get up early.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Past tense: add было. It stays neuter even though Маша is feminine.

sentenceBuilding.translation: We will need to leave tomorrow.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Future tense: add будет in its fixed neuter form.

errorCorrection.sentence: Завтра нам нужно было встать очень рано.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Tomorrow we will need to get up very early.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Завтра' places the necessity in the future, so the tense word is будет: нужно будет встать. Было is the past word, which clashes with 'завтра.' Был (masc) and была (fem) are personal past forms that would need a nominative subject; an impersonal sentence always uses the neuter будет or было. The tense word marks tense only, never gender.

errorCorrection.sentence: Спасибо, но больше нельзя мне помогать, я справлюсь сам.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Thanks, but you don't need to help me anymore; I'll manage on my own.
errorCorrection.explanation: Не надо means 'no need to, you don't have to,' a soft decline that fits thanking someone and saying you'll manage. Нельзя means 'forbidden,' far too strong (and rude) for declining offered help. 'Не можно' is ungrammatical. Нужно ('it is necessary') reverses the meaning. The negation of necessity (не надо / не нужно) is softer than the prohibition нельзя.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мне нужно покупать новый телефон, старый сломался.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I need to buy a new phone; the old one broke.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нужно the verb is an infinitive, and its aspect follows the usual rules. A single specific purchase (the old phone broke, so buy one new one) is perfective: купить. The imperfective покупать would frame buying phones as a repeated habit, which a one-time need does not fit.

minimalPairs.context: Не _____ так говорить, это обижает Лену.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: No need to say that, it hurts Lena.
minimalPairs.explanation: Не надо is the standard soft negation in an impersonal sentence. Не хочет would mean 'does not want,' a personal-subject verb that would need a nominative noun. The frame here is impersonal, so the necessity word надо is correct.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha needed to work a lot.
minimalPairs.explanation: Impersonal sentences use the fixed neuter было in the past, no matter the gender of the dative person. Была would only fit a personal nominative subject like 'Маша была занята.'

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each impersonal sentence by its tense word: present (no было/будет), past (было), or future (будет).

reviewVocab.definition: is necessary / needs to (an impersonal predicative used with an infinitive; takes an optional dative person; slightly more neutral than надо)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Мне нужно идти' слово 'нужно' выражает необходимость.

reviewVocab.definition: needs to / has to (a more casual near-synonym of нужно; same construction)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Антону надо отдохнуть' слово 'надо' выражает необходимость в разговорном стиле.

reviewVocab.definition: no need to (the soft negation of necessity; gentler than the firm нельзя)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Не надо так говорить' это мягкое отрицание: «не обязательно», а не строгий запрет.

reviewVocab.definition: the past было and future будет tense words; in an impersonal sentence they stay in the fixed neuter form and never change for the gender of the dative person
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маше нужно было купить хлеб' слово 'было' несёт прошедшее время и остаётся в среднем роде.
